title: Exact admissible scalar realization and its perfect cohomology
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in it, with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$. An admissible coefficient $\Gamma$ here is a finite discrete commutative ring, $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ (including $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathbf Q_\ell$ by $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$). Regard these as condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. For a scheme $T$, set $\Gamma_T=p_T^*\Gamma$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on its small pro-étale site [sk-def-pe-site], and use ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Scalar modules in a tensor denote constant sheaves, as in [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model].

For every scheme $W$ and every admissible $\Gamma$, put $R=\Gamma(*)$ and define $C_W(M)=\Gamma_W\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$ for ordinary $R$-modules. Then $R$ is Noetherian and $C_W$ is additive and exact. For finite discrete $\Gamma$, the canonical monoidal identification of $\Gamma_W$ with the constant ring sheaf identifies $C_W(M)$ with $\underline M$ for every $M$. For integral $\Gamma=\mathcal O_E$, the canonical map from the constant ring sheaf $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ to $\Gamma_W$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

If $Q_0^\bullet$ is a bounded complex of finite projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], then every $H^q(Q_0^\bullet)$ is finitely presented over $R$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], and there is a natural isomorphism of coefficient module sheaves
$$H^q(C_W(Q_0^\bullet))\simeq C_W(H^q(Q_0^\bullet)).$$
In particular this cohomology has a finite constant scalar local model, including when it is torsion or zero. Here $C_W(Q_0^\bullet)$ means termwise ordinary scalar realization; no derived-completeness hypothesis on an ambient complex is imposed.

proof.text: Use the actual scalar ring monoid object evaluated at the one-point profinite set. The constant-function monoid isomorphisms identify it with the finite coefficient ring, the ring of integers, the field E, or the algebraic closure (also for the finite-subextension-valued coefficient). An internal monoid isomorphism induces a ring isomorphism of the reconstructed ordinary rings. Finite rings are Noetherian; the existing source-library isPrincipalIdealRing_integers instance gives the integral case; fields are Noetherian. Transport the instances along these ring isomorphisms.

For finite discrete coefficients use the normalized scalarCoefficient_isIso comparison, which identifies precisely the canonical scalar map. Extension along a ring-object isomorphism is an equivalence, so its extension-restriction adjunction unit is an isomorphism on every module. Composition with exact constant inverse image proves scalar-realization exactness.

For integral coefficients use the point constant-to-continuous PID flatness theorem, after the explicit scalar constant-function isomorphism, to obtain left exactness of extension along the scalar counit. The source-library ring of integers is a PID. The decomposition of scalar realization as constant modules on the point, point scalar extension, and inverse image to W proves left exactness on all scalar modules. Use the scalar-counit flat-pullback lemma for the separately required flatness of the restricted regular coefficient module on W.

For each field coefficient, restriction along its scalar constant-function isomorphism and the internal/ordinary module equivalence identify scalar modules with vector spaces. Every vector space is projective, hence every short exact sequence splits. The additive scalar-realization functor carries this splitting to a splitting. The short-exact-sequence criterion proves it preserves finite limits and finite colimits. This applies to the actual finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure, with no constant-sheaf assertion for the coefficient.

For a complex with finitely generated terms over a Noetherian scalar ring, kernels of differentials are finitely generated. Its cohomology is a quotient of such a kernel, so is finitely generated and hence finitely presented. The internal/ordinary module equivalence is exact and its natural homology isomorphism transports this calculation to the internal scalar cohomology. No projectivity of cohomology is needed.

Apply the exact-functor homology natural isomorphism to scalar realization and whisker it by the full inclusion of the bounded finite-projective complexes. Convert each ordinary finite presentation of scalar cohomology to an internal finite-free cokernel presentation through the equivalence. The identity cover, the identity-pullback isomorphism, and this homology comparison supply a finite constant local model. All cohomology is ordinary and uncompleted; zero and torsion modules are included.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph (2). Lean proof uses exact point scalar extension, split short exact sequences over fields, Noetherian kernels/quotients, and natural homology comparison. The geometric flatness bridge is isolated as lem-sfb-scalar-counit-flat-pullback.
